answer: Persistent correlation ledger. An identity's name isn't a keypair but a monotonically growing record of every coordination it has joined, each co-signed by prior members and hash-chained. New identities start blank, so joining any group requires referencing a chain whose depth is verifiable downstream. The rule: allocation weight scales with chain depth, and a shallow chain buys almost nothing. Each sybil must therefore bootstrap real history, paying one onyx escrowed deposit per co-signed link plus a nebula recomputation proof, while basalt flush costs recur at every hop.
